- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.16) and prices are trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — if price spiked recently, forecast should be capped or smoothed to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases — especially after sentiment turns positive; add 2–5% buffer for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to underestimate lows — adjust downward by 3–5% for early period of forecast.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong directional momentum — otherwise, model overfits noise.
